questions.stem: A workup on an ill child revealed low levels of complement C3 in her blood. Which one of the following presentations did this child most likely manifest?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Complement proteins function in innate immunity through enzymatic cleavage of C3 to liberate C3b which directly binds to pathogen surfaces.
  • Following C3b insertion, enzyme cascade events result in lysis of the target cell by the membrane attack complex (complement protein scaffold C5–C9) and recruitment of phagocytes by C3a and C5a cleavage products.

questions.stem: Which one of the following leukocytes is considered a “granulocyte”?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

Granulocytes are immune cells that contain granules in their cytoplasms. 

  • These granules are filled with enzymes and other inflammatory mediators which are released upon activation of the granulocytes. 
  • Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are considered granulocytes. 
  • Although both NK cells and NKT cells have granules, they are referred to as large, granular lymphocytes, not granulocytes.

questions.stem: Vaccination operates to generate a humoral immune response to the immunogen(s). Which one of the following represents the critical function of the resultant humoral response in protecting vaccinated patients from future infections by targeted pathogenic agents?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Antibodies generated by the vaccination are produced by antigen-specific memory B cells which reside in the bone marrow.
  • The most critical function of a vaccine-mediated humoral response is to generate antibodies which block attachment of infectious agents to host cell surfaces or neutralization. 
  • This blockade completely inhibits microbial colonization and ensures protection from the pathogen.

questions.stem: An 8-month-old male has recurrent episodes of serious infections including otitis media, chronic sinusitis, and bacterial pneumonia. He is diagnosed with X-linked agammaglobulinemia after an immunologic workup. Which test result is consistent with this diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.text: Absent CD16+ and CD54+ cells in peripheral blood

options.label: B
options.text: Absent CD19+ and CD20+ cells in peripheral blood

options.label: C
options.text: Absent serum IgG, very low levels of IgM

options.label: D
options.text: Decreased CD3+ cells in peripheral blood

questions.answerText: Absent CD19+ and CD20+ cells in peripheral blood
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA), also called Bruton agammaglobulinemia, is a congenital immune deficiency disease characterized by a lack of B-cell production by the bone marrow. B cells express CD19 and CD20, and these two markers are exploited in flow cytometry studies to enumerate B cells in the peripheral blood. The lack of these cells in peripheral blood of a male infant is diagnostic for XLA

questions.stemHtml: The 50-year-old woman has been under the care of an endocrinologist and receiving radioactive iodine for a hyperthyroid condition in which thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins are present in the serum. Clinical image shown here. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • The image shown here depicts  a woman with ophthalmopathy secondary to the hyperthyroidism of Graves disease. 
  • Graves disease is due to the formation of antibodies to the thyroid stimulating hormone receptor. 
  • These antibodies constantly stimulate the thyroid to secrete thyroid hormones in the absence of normal physiological feedback mechanisms that control hormone secretion.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman with chronic joint pain receives a diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis. What pathologic process, ongoing in the synovial membranes of her affected joints, is the most important contributor to joint damage?

options.label: A
options.text: B-cell autoantibody production and immune complex deposition

options.label: C
options.text: Cytokine activation of synoviocytes, chrondocytes, and osteoclasts

options.label: D
options.text: Cytotoxic T cell-mediated destruction of cartilage

questions.answerText: Cytokine activation of synoviocytes, chrondocytes, and osteoclasts
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • RA is considered to be a T helper cell-driven autoimmune disease. 
  • Many of the pathological processes are mediated by T cell derived cytokines which activate joint-associated cells for further cytokine secretion as well as proliferation and enhanced function. 
  • Under the influence of cytokines, the synovial membrane thickens to form a granulation tissue called pannus. Pannus consists of proliferating fibroblast like synoviocytes, as well as infiltrating mononuclear cells. 
  • Cytokines and other mediators activate osteoclasts and chrondrocytes. Activated osteoclasts lead to bone resorption and degradation of bone.

questions.stem: Which of the following laboratory assays can be used to detect the number and types of immune cells in the peripheral blood?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Flow cytometry is a laser-based method used for the analysis of cells and selected cell components. 
  • One of the most popular applications of flow cytometry is immunophenotyping of cell populations. 
  • In this method, single-cell suspensions stream through a flow cell in which the cells pass through a laser beam for sensing. 
  • As the cells pass through the laser, they scatter light. If cells also contain fluorescent molecules, this will be detected. 
  • Both scattered light and fluorescent light information is recorded and analyzed to identify subpopulations within the sample

questions.stem: A 9-month-old male with a history of recurrent, serious extracellular bacterial infections is hospitalized with pneumonia due to Pneumocystis jiroveci. An immunologic workup reveals neutropenia, normal numbers of T and B cells, normal complement levels and complement activity, elevated IgM and very low IgG and IgA. What is the molecular defect in this disease?

options.label: A
options.text: Defective expression by lymphocytes of adenosine deaminase

options.label: C
options.text: Mutation of the NADPH oxidase enzyme

options.label: D
options.text: Reduced expression of CD154 on T cells

questions.answerText: Reduced expression of CD154 on T cells
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • This case is descriptive of hyper-IgM syndrome, a disease whose molecular defect is caused by mutations in the gene for CD40 ligand otherwise known as CD154. 
  • The case describes a child with T-cell dysfunction, as demonstrated by his infection with Pneumocystis jeroveci a fungal organism thought to be part of the normal oropharyngeal flora and that causes disease in patients with compromised T-cell–mediated immunity. 
  • As the T cells are normal in number, their activation must be impaired, and his current infection supports this idea. 
  • The fact that the patient has elevated IgM and very low levels of IgG and IgA, suggests that the T cells cannot interact adequately with B cells to induce class switching. In addition to cytokine stimuli, the interaction of CD40 on the B cell with CD40 ligand (also known as CD154) on the T cell is essential to stimulate class switching in B cells

  • Cryptic antigens are the antigenic epitopes, which are normally not exposed, gets exposed to the immune system as a result of injury or infection and leads to development of immune response.
  • Inappropriate expression of MHC proteins also leads to development of self-destructive immune response.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man develops an abscess on the back of his neck. Culture yields S. aureus. The isolate is tested and found to be positive for the mecA gene, which means that

options.label: C
options.text: The isolate is resistant to nafcillin.

options.text: The isolate is resistant to clindamycin

questions.answerText: The isolate is resistant to nafcillin.
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) mecA genes expressed in MRSA. Resistance to nafcillin (and oxacillin and methicillin) occurs in about 65% of S. aureus isolates. Nafcillin resistance correlates with the presence of mecA or mecC, the genes that encode for a penicillin binding protein (PBP2a) not affected by these drugs. Resistance to penicillin G can be predicted by a positive test result for β-lactamase; approximately 90% of S. aureus produce β-lactamase.

questions.stem: Which one of the following best describes the pathogenesis of acute rheumatic fever?

options.label: A
options.text: An exotoxin produced by Streptococcus pyogenes that acts as a superantigen damages cardiac muscle.

options.label: B
options.text: An exotoxin produced by Streptococcus pyogenes thatADPribosylates a G protein damages joint tissue.

options.label: C
options.text: Antibody to the capsular polysaccharide of Streptococcus pyogenes cross-reacts with joint tissue and damages it.

options.label: D
options.text: Antibody to the M protein of Streptococcus pyogenes cross reacts with cardiac muscle and damages it.

questions.answerText: Antibody to the M protein of Streptococcus pyogenes cross reacts with cardiac muscle and damages it.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Rheumatic fever is due to an immunologic cross-reaction between antibodies formed against M proteins of S. pyogenes and proteins on the surface of joint, heart, and brain tissue. 
  • It is an autoimmune disease greatly exacerbated by recurrent streptococcal infections. 
  • If streptococcal infections are treated within 8 days of onset, rheumatic fever is usually prevented. 
  • After a heart-damaging attack of rheumatic fever, reinfection must be prevented by long-term prophylaxis.

  • Gonococci produces Penicillinase. (PPNG)
  • No vaccine for gonococci.
  • Neisseria gonorrhoeae (gonococcus) has multiple serotypes based on the antigenicity of its pilus protein. 
  • There is marked antigenic variation in the gonococcal pili as a result of chromosomal rearrangement; more than 100 serotypes are known.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with bilateral pneumonia. HisLegionella urinary antigen test result is positive. Which of the following is the likely cause of his pneumonia?

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above because the urinary antigen test is genusspecific and not species or serotype specific.

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Antigenic specificity of L. pneumophila is thought to be attributable to complex antigenic structures. 
  • There are at least 16 serogroups of L. pneumophila; serogroup 1 was the cause of the 1976 outbreak of Legionnaires’ disease and remains themost common serogroup isolated from humans. 
  • Legionella species cannot be identified by serogrouping alone because there is cross-reactive antigenicity among different species. 
  • The Legionella urinary antigen test may be used early in the course of infection with L. pneumophila serogroup 1 and is very helpful when the result ispositive.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: They are used as alternatives to the tuberculin skin test to evaluate for latent tuberculosis.

questions.answerText: They are used as alternatives to the tuberculin skin test to evaluate for latent tuberculosis.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Sometimes the results of the tuberculin skin test are equivocal, particularly in persons who have been vaccinated with BCG or who live in areas where NTM are highly prevalent in the environment. 
  • In an effort to improve diagnostic accuracy, whole-blood interferon-γ release assays (IGRAs) have been commercially developed. 
  • These assays are based on the host’s immune responses to specific M. tuberculosis antigens ESAT-6 (early secretory antigenic target-6) and CFP-10.
  • The tuberculin skin test or the IGRAs can be used to screen persons for latent tuberculosis infection

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Of newborns infected by the mother, 10–20% may develop respiratory tract involvement 2–12 weeks after birth, culminating in pneumonia. Interstitial infiltrates and hyperinflation can be seen on radiographs. The diagnosis should be suspected if pneumonitis develops in a newborn who has inclusion conjunctivitis and can be established by isolation of C. trachomatis from respiratory secretions.

questions.stemHtml: A 52-year-old NRI man presents for evaluation of a lesion on his right hand, which initially appeared 4 days ago as a raised red bump. He denies trauma to the hand, other than a tick bite that he noticed last week. He also reports 3 days of headache, fatigue, myalgias and diaphoresis. He has no chronic medical conditions, takes no medications, lives alone, and has no pets. He works as a park ranger at a nearby state park and likes to hike and hunt in his spare time. He eats a balanced diet of fruits, vegetables, eggs, and wild game. Physical exam is notable for a moderately ill-appearing man with tender lymphadenopathy of the right axilla, with overlying erythema. Temperature is 102°F, blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 109/min, and respirations are 21/min. A photograph of the patient’s right hand is shown in the image. Which is the most likely causative agent of this patient’s illness?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • This patient with an ulcerative lesion, local lymphadenopathy, fever, and nonspecific systemic symptoms (headache, myalgias, and fatigue) after a tick bite most likely has tularemia, caused by Fransicella tularensis. 
  • Fransicella tularensis is a zoonotic bacteria.
  • It is spread by contact with small mammals (rabbits, mice, and squirrels) or insect vectors (ticks or deer flies). 
  • The acute illness that develops, called tularemia (also known as “rabbit fever”) can take different forms, depending on the bacteria’s portal of entry.
  • Ulceroglandular and glandular tularemia are the most common, both occur after skin inoculation via an animal/insect bite. Uncommon forms include occuloglandular, pharyngeal, pneumonic, and typhoidal. 
  • Ulceroglandular tularemia, the form seen in this patient, presents with nonspecific systemic symptoms (e.g. headache, body aches, and fatigue), fever, a characteristic skin lesion (a pustule that ulcerates and may develop a central eschar), and tender, erythematous regional lymphadenopathy. 
  • The diagnosis may be confirmed with serology, but treatment should be started empirically with an aminoglycoside (e.g., streptomycin, gentamicin), a fluoroquinolone (e.g., ciprofloxacin), or a tetracycline

questions.stem: A 6-day-old boy is brought to the emergency department due to inability to feed for 12 hours. The parents report that he has been unable to open his mouth and has had clenched hands all day. The neonate was delivered at home by the grandmother. After the umbilical cord was cut with a kitchen knife, the parents rubbed a coin on the umbilical stump to promote wealth during the child's life as is customary in their culture. The mother did not undergo prenatal care but says the pregnancy was uncomplicated. Physical examination shows increased muscle tone throughout, arching of the back, and dorsiflexed feet. In addition to hygienic umbilical cord care, which of the following interventions would have most likely prevented this neonate's condition?

options.label: C
options.text: Vaccination of the mother during pregnancy

options.label: D
options.text: Vaccination of the neonate at birth

questions.answerText: Vaccination of the mother during pregnancy
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • It’s a case of neonatal tetanus caused by Clostridium tetani.
  • It occurs when Clostridium tetani spores are introduced to the neonate, generally from unhygienic delivery or cord care. 
  • Symptoms typically begin 5-7 days after birth and can progress more rapidly than in adults.
  • Infected neonates become irritable and have difficulty feeding/suckling due to tonic spasm of the masticatory muscles (trismus). 
  • As the disease progresses, spasms and hypertonicity become more generalized. 
  • Mortality approaches 100% without treatment.
  • Prevention of neonatal tetanus is achieved primarily by vaccination of the mother during pregnancy with an inactivated tetanus toxin (tetanus toxoid) as part of the tetanus-diptheria (Td) vaccine. 
  • An appropriately vaccinated woman provides transplacental IgG to the fetus, which decreases the incidence of neonatal tetanus by approximately 95%

questions.answerText: Altered structure of enzymes involved in bacterial RNA synthesis
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Most cases of pulmonary tuberculosis are initially treated with a combination of 4 drugs (RIPE therapy):
  • Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide and Ethambutol
  • Although each of these medications can cause adverse effects, harmless red-orange discoloration of body fluids (eg, urine, sweat, saliva, tears) is typically caused by a rifamycin. Rifamycins exert their effect by blocking DNAdependent RNA polymerase, which prevents bacterial transcription and subsequent protein synthesis; resistance typically arises due to mutations that result in structural alterations of the enzyme

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman comes to the office with a one-week history of painful swelling in her right axilla that was preceded by malaise, headaches, and night sweats. Temperature is 37.8 deg C, blood pressure is 126/78 mm Hg, and pulse is 88/min. Physical examination shows enlarged and tender epitrochlear and axillary lymph nodes on the right side. Histopathologic examination of a lymph node shows scattered necrotizing granulomas and stellate micro abscesses containing pleomorphic, gram-negative coccobacilli. Which of the following is the most likely route of transmission of this patient’s infection?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • This patient with tender axillary and epitrochlear lymphadenopathy has histopathologic findings consistent with cat scratch disease, caused by Bartonella henselae infection. 
  • B henselae is a fastidious, gram-negative coccobacillus that is transmitted to humans (typically children and young adults) through a scratch or bite from an infected cat.
  • A skin lesion (eg, erythematous papule, vesicle) usually forms at the inoculation site (eg, hand, arm) within days of the scratch; however, this lesion may go unnoticed. 
  • Within weeks, patients develop tender lymphadenopathy proximal to the skin lesion (eg, axillary, epitrochlear). 
  • Additional symptoms may include fever, malaise, aches, and night sweats. 
  • The diagnosis is often made clinically and confirmed with serologic testing, but biopsy of the affected lymph node may be performed in some cases. 
  • Histopathology often shows necrotizing granulomas and stellate shaped micro-abscesses (ie, collections of neutrophils). 
  • A silver stain (eg, Warthin-Starry) can be used to highlight the organisms

questions.stem: Which of the following is the metabolically active form of Chlamydia trachomatis?

questions.stem: A 36-year-old soldier suffered a gun-shot wound to the abdomen that required an emergent exploratory laparotomy to repair and resect damaged portions of the bowel. Four days later, the patient reports increased generalized abdominal pain. Physical exam reveals rebound tenderness, worse in the bilateral lower quadrants. The surgical and bullet-entrance wounds appear intact without any evidence of leakage/drainage, erythema, or warmth. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a 4 cm abscess in the left lower quadrant. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this patient's current presentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • This patient is suffering from an intra-abdominal infection. Bacterial infections in the abdomen are typically polymicrobial, with Bacteroides fragilis and Escherichia coli as the two most common organisms. 
  • B. fragilis is an anaerobic Gram-negative rod that is found as part of the normal gastrointestinal tract flora. 
  • An abdominal infection with this organism often results from endogenous transmission from the gut due to either abdominal trauma or emergency abdominal surgery. It may be treated with metronidazole, clindamycin, or cefoxitin; however, abscesses should be surgically drained when possible.

questions.stemHtml: A 9-year old child was admitted in NICU with meningitis. No history of childhood vaccinations. The organism isolated from CSF exhibits a property shown in the image. What is factor needed to demonstrate this property?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Organism causing meningitis is Hemophilus influenzae.
  • The property shown in the image is satellitism.
  • Blood agar medium provides only an X-factor, but for obtaining a V-factor, the erythrocytes present in the blood agar must be haemolyzed. 
  • H. influenzae can neither haemolyze the blood nor grow without the V-factor, so H. influenzae alone can’t grow in a blood agar medium. 
  • Staphylococcus aureus is hemolytic, and its presence in the blood agar medium makes V-factor (NAD) available in the medium. Hence, H. influenzae can grow in the vicinity of S. aureus colonies in the blood agar medium. This phenomenon is called ‘satellitism

questions.stem: A 48-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4 count of 40 complains of memory loss to his doctor. Four months later, he becomes paralyzed and dies. questions.stem: A 4-month-old child develops a viral infection with fever and vesicular lesions in the anterior portion of the mouth, as well as around the mouth.   • The case describes gingivostomatitis due to herpes simplex virus type 1. 
  • The most common age for acquisition of HSV-1 is during early childhood, and the most common clinical manifestation of primary infection in young children is gingivostomatitis. 
  • The virus is most commonly transmitted to young children from caregivers with apparent or inapparent shedding of recurrent virus. 
  • Thus, the mother transmitted HSV-1 to the child when she had the cold sore. 
  • Following recovery from gingivostomatitis, the child remains infected with HSV-1. 
  • The virus remains latent in ganglia through out life and can periodically reactivate to cause cold sores or be shed asymptomatically.

questions.stem: Yellow fever still exists in many tropical areas of the globe. Which one of the following is the best reason yellow fever still exists?

options.label: A
options.text: Sewage disposal is inadequate in many areas.

options.label: B
options.text: Both humans and monkeys are reservoirs for yellow fever virus.

options.label: C
options.text: The virus has mutated, so the existing vaccine is no longer effective.

options.label: D
options.text: The vaccine has been withdrawn because it was found to have unacceptable side effects.

questions.answerText: Both humans and monkeys are reservoirs for yellow fever virus.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Yellow fever occurs primarily in the tropical areas of Africa and South America. 
  • In the epidemiology of yellow fever, two distinct cycles exist in nature, with different reservoirs and vectors.
  • Jungle yellow fever is a disease of monkeys in tropical Africa and South America; it is transmitted primarily by thetreetop mosquitoes of the Haemagogus species. 
  • Monkeys are the permanent reservoir, whereas humans are accidental hosts. Humans (e.g., tree cutters) are infected when they enter thejungle occupationally.
  • Urban yellow fever is a disease of humans that is transmitted by the mosquito Aedes aegypti, which breeds in stagnant water. In the urban form of the disease, humans are the reservoir. 
  • For effective transmission to occur, the virus must replicate in the mosquito during the 12- to 14-day extrinsic incubation period. 
  • After the infected mosquito bites the person, the intrinsic incubation period is 3 to 6 days.

  • The other is a live reassortant vaccine (Rotateq), which contains five rotavirus strains (G1, G2, G3, G4, and G9). 
  • An increased risk of intussusception has been reported with both vaccines. 
  • Patients with a history of intussusception should not receive either vaccines

  • Vector is female Anopheles mosquito.
  • Infective stage is sporozoite.
  • Diagnostic stages are trophozoite and gametocytes.
  • No hypnozoites stage in P. falciparum and No relapse also.

questions.stem: All the following statements regarding Toxoplasma gondii are false except

options.label: A
options.text: One way to prevent this infection is to advise pregnant women not to drink unpasteurized milk.

options.label: B
options.text: The form of Toxoplasma found in the tissue cysts in humans is the rapidly dividing tachyzoite.

options.label: C
options.text: The most important definitive host for Toxoplasma is the domestic cat.

options.label: D
options.text: Infection in people with reduced cell-mediated immunity, such as AIDS patients, is characterized by persistent watery diarrhea

questions.answerText: The most important definitive host for Toxoplasma is the domestic cat.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Toxoplasmosis – Cat is the definitive host.
  • In tissues, it become brady cyst.
  • All stages are infective to human.
  • It causes cerebral toxoplasmosis in PLHIV and Congenital toxoplasmosis.
  • Treatment : Sulfadiazine with Pyrimethamine.

questions.stemHtml: A 25-year-old man with fever and weight loss for the past 3 weeks. Physical exam was noncontributory. Laboratory tests revealed anemia and leukopenia. Multiple blood cultures for bacteria and fungi were negative, as was a test for the p24 antigen of HIV. Computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen revealed splenomegaly. A bone marrow biopsy was performed, and a stained sample revealed the pathogen as shown in the image. Of the following, which one is the most likely cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Image shown here is amastigotes inside the macrophages suggestive of Leishmaniasis. 
  • Caused by L. donovoni and vector is sandfly.
  • Treatment – Amphotericin B

questions.stem: Agent causing Chiclero’s ulcer is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Chiclero ulcer caused by L. mexicana.
  • Espundia caused by > brasiliensis
  • L. tropica causes Cutaneous leishmaniasis.

questions.stem: Ideal animal model used for cultivation of Leishmania donovani is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Leishmania donovani is inoculated into Hamsters.
  • Intranasal inoculation of specimens to golden hamsters yields amastigotes after several months .
  • This method is currently not in use.

questions.stemHtml: Clinical image shown here is diagnosed as Winterbottom sign. Name the vector for this pathogen.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Winterbottom sign is the feature of African sleeping sickness caused by T. brucei.
  • Vector is Tsetse fly and mode of transmission is bite.

questions.stem: Protozoa exhibits reversion motility is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Balantidium coli exhibits football motility or reversion motility.
  • Trichomonas – Twitching / jerky motility
  • Giardia – Falling leaf motility
  • Entamoeba – Amoeboid motility

questions.stemHtml: Image shown here acts as vector for transmission for all the following parasitic infections except
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Image shown here is cyclops.
  • It act as a vector for D. latum, D. medinensis and G. spinigerum.
  • Vector for Babesiosis is Hard tick.

questions.stem: House fly acts as mechanical vector for all the following infections except
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Neurocysticercosis is caused by Taenia solium.
  • It is not a vector borne disease.
  • It is due to ingestion of Hexacanth egg of T. solium.

questions.stem: Calabar swelling is caused by
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Calabar swelling caused by Loa loa.
  • Th is is the most common form of loiasis, also called as fugitive swelling 
  • It is a subcutaneous swelling developing on the extremities (knee or wrist) and less frequently at other sites
  • Swelling develops rapidly in few hours, preceded by localized pain, pruritus and urticaria and last for 3–4 days

questions.stem: Sheathed microfilaria seen in all the following except
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Sheathed microfilaria seen in Loa loa, Brugia malayi and Wuchereria bancrofti.

questions.stem: All the following causes auto infection except
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Autoinfection caused by H. nana, T. solium, E. vermicularis, C. parvum and S. stercoralis.

questions.stemHtml: A child admitted with the complaints of diarrhoea. Stool examination revealed the pathogen as shown in the image.Choose the complication lead by this pathogen.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Image shown here depicts Trichuris trichiura egg.
  • Complication in children – rectal prolapse
  • In adults – Iron deficiency anaemia.

questions.stem: Rhabditiform larva is diagnostic stage in
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Rhabditiform larva is diagnostic stage of Strongyloides stercoralis.
  • Human excretes rhabditiform larva in stool.
  • It causes autoinfection and hyper infection syndrome.
  • Treatment – Ivermectin.

questions.stemHtml: A 32-year-old male tourist traveled to Senegal for 1 month. During the trip, he swam in the Gambia River. Two months after his return, he began complaining of intermittent lower abdominal pain with dysuria. Laboratory results of ova and parasites revealed eggs as shown in the image. Choose the correct infective stage of this pathogen.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Image shown here is egg with terminal spine suggestive of Schistosoma hematobium.
  • Infective stage is Cercariae with bifurcated tail.
  • Mode of transmission – Skin penetration.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man admitted with the complains of pain abdomen, jaundice with increased alkaline phosphatase and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia: USG shows blockade of the biliary tree. Stool examination revealed operculated eggs. What could be the cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Operculated egg suggestive of trematodes.
  • Pain abdomen, jaundice with increased alkaline phosphatase and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. USG shows blockadeof the biliary tree. Suggestive of infection by Clonorchis sinensis infection.
  • Moderate to heavy infection may be associated with vague right-upper-quadrant pain.
  • Chronic or repeated infection is associated with manifestations such as Cholangitis, cholangiohepatitis, and biliaryobstruction

questions.stem: Which organism egg can be isolated from stool andsputum?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Eggs of Paragonimus westermanii can be isolated from stool and sputum. It causes endemic hemoptysis.

questions.stem: Arc-5 in CIEP is diagnostic for
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Immunodiffusion and counter current electrophoresis (CIEP) are used for hydatid disease: Detecting antibody againstantigen-5 (arc-5)
  • Western blot: Detecting antibody against antigen B fragment
  • Antibody methods are useful for sero-epidemiological study but cannot differentiate recent and past infection.

questions.stem: Choose the correct statement about fish tape worm.

options.label: A
options.text: Cattle are the most important intermediate hosts.

options.label: B
options.text: Megaloblastic anemia may occur as a result of vitamin B12 deficiency.

options.label: C
options.text: The laboratory diagnosis depends on finding a scolex with hooklets in the stool.

options.label: D
options.text: Infection is acquired by the ingestion of eggs in food or water contaminated with human feces.

questions.answerText: Megaloblastic anemia may occur as a result of vitamin B12 deficiency.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Fish tapeworm – Diphyllobothrium latum.
  • It causes megaloblastic anaemia.
  • Operculated egg in stool is diagnostic.

questions.stem: Neurocysticercosis is most likely to be acquired by

options.label: A
options.text: Drinking water contaminated with feces of an infected human

options.label: B
options.text: Drinking water contaminated with feces of an infected pig.

options.label: C

options.text: Ingestion of undercooked pork from an infected pig.

questions.answerText: Drinking water contaminated with feces of an infected human
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Neurocysticercosis caused by Taenia solium.
  • Infective stage – Hexacanth egg – contaminated water/ food by human feces.
  • Cysticercus cellulosae also an infective stage by consumption of contaminated pork meat

questions.stem: Second intermediate host for Clonorchis sinensis is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Fish is the second intermediate host for Clonorchis sinensis.
  • Crab – P. westermanii
  • Plant – F. buski and F. hepatica

questions.stem: Larva currens is caused by
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Larva currens caused by S. stercoralis.
  • Migrating larvae may produce the pathognomonic serpiginous urticarial rash called as larva currensthat advances as fast as 10 cm/hour.
  • Urticaria and perianal involvement present.

questions.stem: In which of the following trematode, the sexes are separate?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • In Schistosoma sexes are separate.
  • Other trematodes are hermaphrodites.

questions.stemHtml: A 42-year-old man with fever, myalgia, and facial swelling. White blood cell count was 14,400 with 24% eosinophils. Additional history reveals that he shot a bear in hunting and ate some of it about 6 weeks ago. He emphasized that he likes his meat rare. A muscle biopsy was performed, and a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain of the tissue shown in the image. Of the following, which one is the most likely cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Image shown here is nurse cell of Trichinella spiralis.
  • Encysted larva in striated muscles.

questions.stemHtml: A 35-year-old woman admitted with severe upper abdominal pain for the past hour. There is no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Physician suspecting cholecystitis, pancreatitis, or a perforated viscus but first ask her if she has ingested raw fish recently. She says yes and tells that she had sashimi the night before last. Endoscopy reveals a larva in the gastric mucosa as shown in the image. Of the following, which one is the most likely cause?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Anisakiasis is caused by the larvae of the nematode, Anisakis simplex. 
  • The larvae are ingested in raw seafood and can penetrate the submucosa of the stomach or intestine. 
  • The adult worms live in the intestines of marine mammals such as whales, dolphins, and seals. 
  • The eggs produced by the adults are eaten by crustaceans, which are then eaten by marine fish such as salmon, mackerel, and herring. 
  • Gastroenteritis, abdominal pain, eosinophilia, and occult blood in the stool typically occur. 
  • Acute infection can resemble appendicitis, and chronic infection can resemble gastrointestinal cancer.

questions.stem: RBC’s are enlarged in infection with
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) RBC size: Enlarged in –P. vivax and P. ovlae, others- normal size • RBC shape: Oval in P. ovale, others- round

questions.stemHtml: A 16-Year-old complains of loose motion, intermittent abdominal pain of 1-year. wet mount of stool shows multiple ova > 100 microns in length as shown in the image. Which of the following agent is responsible for this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Among the options, eggs of Fasciola Gigantica are larger > 100 µm size and Fasciola Gigantica is associated with fever and abdominalsymptoms.
  • Eggs are oval, bile stained, unembryonated and operculated, larger in size (160–190 µm × 70–90 µm).
  • Acute disease develops during metacercariae migration (1–2 weeks after infection) and includes fever, right-upper-quadrant pain, hepatomegaly and eosinophilia.

questions.stemHtml: A 42-year-old neutropenic patient admitted with hemoptysis and pneumonia. Sputum microscopy shown in the image. Choose the correct statement regarding this pathogen.

questions.answerText: The clinical manifestations include local infections of the ear, cornea, nails, and sinuses.

questions.stem: Ectothrix is due to

questions.stem: A 25 years old female complains of recurrent rhinitis, nasal discharge and bilateral nasal blockage for past 2 years. She has history of asthma and allergy. On examination multiple ethmoidal polyps are noted with mucosal thickening and impacted secretions in both the nasal cavities. Biopsy is taken and the material is cultured which shown the growth of many septate hyphae with dichotomous branching typically at 45 deg angle. Invasiveness of this pathogen determined by which of the following test?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • The history provided in the question, suggests involvement of paranasal sinuses with presence of multiple ethmoidalpolyps in an asthmatic patient.
  • Septate hyphae with dichotomous branching typically at 45° is observed in morphology of Filamentous fungi Aspergillus.
  • Invasiveness is assessed by Galactomannan assay.

questions.stemHtml: A vitreous aspirate from a case of metastatic endophthalmitis on culture yields Gram-positive round to oval cells, 12-14 µm in size. The aspirate on Gram staining shows the presence of pseudohyphae. It exhibits a property shown in the image. Which of the following is the most likely etiological agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • The history provided suggests that it is a case of disseminated fungal endophthalmitis.
  • The fungal agent has morphology of yeast cells with pseudohyphae suggests diagnosis of Candida spp
  • Image shown here is germ tube test which is positive for Candida albicans.

questions.stem: Mycotoxin causing liver cancer is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Aflatoxin produced by Aspergillus flavus, Aspergillus parasiticus, A.nomius.
  • Source is Nuts and  Maize
  • It causes Hepatoma, Hepatitis, Indian childhood cirrhosis, Reye’s syndrome

questions.stemHtml: A 30 year old rose Gardner came with the complaints of ulcers in hand as shown in the image. Based on the clinical diagnosis, choose the correct statement regarding this pathogen.

options.label: A
options.text: The main reservoir is dog feces.

options.label: B
options.text: Laboratory diagnosis involves seeing a non-septate mold in an aspirate of the lesion.

options.label: C
options.text: It is often acquired by penetrating wounds sustained while gardening.

options.label: D
options.text: Disease occurs primarily in patients who are deficient in the late-acting complement components.

questions.answerText: It is often acquired by penetrating wounds sustained while gardening.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Ulcers and nodules along lymphatic drainage suggestive of sporotrichosis.
  • Rose gardeners' disease. 
  • It is often acquired by penetrating wounds sustained while gardening.
  • Treatment – Itraconazole.

questions.stemHtml: A 28-year-old PLHIV came with pain in the hip region. Aspiration stained with Giemsa staining shown in the image. The organism might be
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Image shown here is Giemsa staining shows multiple monocytes and macrophages with yeast like organism in the cytoplasm of cells suggestive of Histoplasma capsulatum.
  • It’s a Case of osteomyelitis in PLHIV  caused by H. capsulatum.
  • Dimorphic fungi resides in reticulo endothelial system.

questions.stem: All the following are causing endemic mycosis except
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Endemic or systemic mycosis caused by Coccidioides, Paracoccidioides, Histoplasma and Blastomyces.
  • They confined to a particular geographical area, so named as endemic mycosis.

questions.stem: All the following are dimorphic fungi except
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Thermally dimorphic fungi exists in two forms. Based on the temperature, they change their morphology.
  • At 37 deg, in tissues – Yeast form and at 25 deg in environment – Mold form.
  • Sporothrix, Talaromyces and all systemic mycosis are examples for dimorphic fungi.

questions.stem: Most common fungal infection seen in febrile neutropenia is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • Febrile neutropenia- Fever more than 38.5°C and absolute neutrophil count less than 500/µl.
  • Neutrophils/CMI play crucial role in controlling Candida infection, hence deep seated and disseminated Candidainfections are common in Neutropenic patients

questions.stemHtml: A 30-year-old PLHIV female presents with difficulty in swallowing. On examination, curdy white material seen on the tongue. Microscopy of the scrapping shown in the image. The probable cause is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • PLHIV and curdy white material on tongue suggestive of oral thrush.
  • Image shown here is pseudohyphae confirms of invasive candidiasis.
  • Caused by Candida albicans.

questions.stem: Specific stain used to demonstrate Cryptococcus neoformans is
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Cryptococcus neoformans is carminiphilic fungi.
  • Specific stain used to demonstrate Cryptococcus is mucicarmine stain.
  • India ink and nigrosin stain are negative stains used to demonstrate the capsule

questions.stemHtml: Patient came with hypopigmented lesions on the back. Microscopy shown in the image. Choose the correct etiological agent.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Image shown here is spaghetti meat ball appearance.
  • It’s a case of Tinea versicolor caused by Malassezia furfur.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes mellitusdeveloped a bloody nasal discharge, facial edema, and necrosis of his nasal septum. Culture of his cloudy nasal secretions yielded Rhizopus species. What is the most important implication of this finding?

options.label: A
options.text: No diagnostic value because this mold is an airborne contaminant.

options.label: D
options.text: The patient has been exposed to indoor mold contamination.

questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (B)

  • It’s a case of rhinocerebral mucormycosis caused by Rhizopus.
  • Seen in DKA, Dialysis and Desferroxamine therapy.
  • Treatment – Amphotericin B and surgery.

questions.stem: Choose the correct statement regarding tinea infection.

options.label: A
options.text: The dermatophytes are molds and are not thermally dimorphic.

options.label: B
options.text: The drug of choice for the treatment of ringworm lesions is amphotericin B.

options.label: C
options.text: The purpose of the KOH prep is to observe fungal antigens within infected cells.

options.label: D
options.text: The dermatophytid reaction refers to the necrotic area typically seen in the center of ringworm lesions.

questions.answerText: The dermatophytes are molds and are not thermally dimorphic.

Correct Answer (A)

  • Tinea infection caused by dermatophytes – Cutaneous mycosis
  • Keratophilic molds.
  • KOH mount used to see fungal elements clearly.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman who is in her third trimester of pregnancy, from California complains of severe low back pain of several weeks in duration. An X-ray reveals a lesion in the fourth lumbar vertebra. Material from a needle biopsy of the lesion is examined by a pathologist who calls to tell you the patient has coccidioidomycosis. Of the following, which one did the pathologist see inthe biopsy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Coccidioides immitis causes coccidiomycosis.
  • Dimorphic fungi.
  • Yeast form in tissues – Spherule containing endospores.
  • Mold form – Arthroconidia.

questions.stemHtml: A 36 year old man admitted with wart like lesions in the leg. Biopsy sent for HPE. Microscopy image shown here. Choose the correct clinical diagnosis.
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • Wart like lesions and HPE shows Copper penny / sclerotic bodies suggestive of Chromoblastomycosis.
  • Sub cutaneous fungal infections.
  • Caused by Phialophora, Cladospora and Fonsecaea.

questions.stem: Which one of the following pathogenic yeasts is not a common member of the normal human flora or microbiota?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (C)

  • Cryptococcus neoformans is not a commensal microbe.
  • MCC fungal meningitis in PLHIV.

questions.stemHtml: A 52-year-old PLHIV admitted with fever, dyspnea, nonproductive cough,and moderate chest pain. His history includes noncompliance with HAART. His CD4 count is 100/ cmm. Chest radiographs reveal diffuse bilateral infiltrates. Lactate dehydrogenase levels are elevated. Cyst like structures are recovered in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid as shown in the image. Which of the following antimicrobial agents represents the best treatment option for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (D)

  • This case is descriptive of pneumocystis pneumonia. Pneumocystis jiroveci is the causative agent of this condition. 
  • The image depicts the cystic stage of the organism.
  • It is found in the respiratory tracts of healthy individuals where its growth is controlled by macrophages.
  • Without sufficient CD4+ cells that secrete γ-interferon to activate macrophages, these phagocytic cells will have difficulty in killing the microbe. Pneumocystis infection can be prevented by TMP/SMZ given prophylactically to HIV-infected individuals with CD4 counts of less than 200/cmm. 
  • The patient in this case was noncompliant with medication, thereby increasing his risk for this and other opportunistic infections

questions.stem: A 24-year-old farmer, presents with difficulty in vision in the left eye for the last 10 days. He is immunocompetent from a rural community and gives history of trauma to his left eye with vegetative matter 10–15 days back. On examinations, there is an ulcerative lesion in the cornea, whose base has raised soft creamy infiltrate. Ulcer margin is feathery and hyphae. Branching aseptate hyphae were noted. There are a few satellite lesions also. Corneal scrapping shows sickle shaped macro conidia. What should be the probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct Answer (A)

  • Fusarium is a hyaline filamentous fungi, may cause a range of opportunistic infections in humans.
  • In humans with normal immune systems, fusarial infections may occur in the nails (onychomycosis) and in the cornea (keratomycosis or mycotic keratitis)
  • Diagnosed by presence of sickle shaped macroconidia.
